medical.title: Mental health diagnoses rise with medical complexity, chronicity in children
medical.summary: The prevalence of mental health (MH) diagnoses increases with increasing medical complexity and chronicity in Medicaid-enrolled children, according to a study published in Pediatrics.

medical.title: Flu vaccine effectiveness often weaker than advertised, study finds
medical.summary: New research suggests health officials may be overselling the protective power of the annual flu shot—but that doesn't mean folks should skip it, researchers added. The new analysis finds the influenza vaccine is often less protective than the 40% to 60% effectiveness against infection that's routinely stated, according to researchers from the University of Maryland.

medical.title: Your genes might boost risk for high cholesterol
medical.summary: Frustrated that your cholesterol levels aren't budging for the better? You may have your genes to blame, a new study finds.

medical.title: Hair pulling, skin picking and nail biting are common in young people and cause significant distress
medical.summary: The study found that body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs), as they are known, can be a significant source of distress, particularly among young people who also experienced anxiety, depression and bullying.

medical.title: Less than half of TikTok videos on RSV prevention offer high-quality info, paper notes
medical.summary: Many people rely on social media to learn more about health conditions and trends. A study published in Vaccine that examined TikTok videos about respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention—including the maternal vaccine (Abrysvo) and the long-acting antibody nirsevimab (Beyfortus) for infants—finds that only 47% present high-quality information.

medical.title: Researchers uncover the mechanisms of adhesion formation after thoracic surgery
medical.summary: Intrathoracic adhesions can develop after thoracic surgery and increase the risk of complications during repeat surgery. However, the detailed molecular mechanisms underlying their formation have remained unclear. In a Letter published in Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy, a team from Japan aimed to establish an animal model that closely reproduces pleural adhesions seen in patients and to identify key cells and signaling pathways involved in adhesion formation. The goal was to find new methods to prevent adhesions after thoracic surgery.

medical.title: Patients give dental implants high marks after 40 years
medical.summary: Nearly 40 years after receiving dental implants and crowns, patients remain highly satisfied with how well they function. Their views on appearance are more mixed, according to a study from the University of Gothenburg, Sweden.

medical.title: Improved mapping reveals location of small molecules in the brain
medical.summary: Hsi-Chun Chao, a postdoctoral researcher at the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, developed a new methodology to map the locations of and differentiate nearly identical molecules in the brain.

medical.title: Metastatic pancreatic cancer responds well to treatment with combination of daraxonrasib and chemotherapy
medical.summary: Daraxonrasib combined with chemotherapy caused substantial tumor shrinkage in patients with pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body, according to new results from a Phase I/II clinical trial.

medical.title: Heart rhythm data reveal early signs of heart disease before conventional measures
medical.summary: The heart does not beat like a regular clock. Even at rest, the time between successive heartbeats continuously varies. Researchers at Tampere and Stanford universities have shown that the patterns of these subtle variations can reveal the early effects of cardiomyopathy, which is a hereditary heart disease. The paper is published in the journal Circulation: Arrhythmia and Electrophysiology.

medical.title: Immune aging blueprint offers new clues to fighting cancer
medical.summary: A new study from Monash University has uncovered a genetic blueprint of immune aging, shedding light on why our bodies become less effective at fighting cancer and infections as we grow older. Published in Science Immunology, the preclinical study identified genetic changes that cause aging immune cells to become less effective, helping to explain why older people are more susceptible to cancer and experience more frequent and severe infections.

medical.title: Nearly half of adults over 70 benefited from exercise training across several areas of physical function
medical.summary: A yearlong exercise program improved physical function among adults aged over 70, but the benefits varied considerably between individuals. A study conducted at the University of Jyväskylä highlights that the success of exercise interventions should not be evaluated using a single outcome measure, as positive changes may occur in different aspects of physical function.

medical.title: Cell biologists uncover key mechanism behind a rare cause of childhood epilepsy
medical.summary: University of Liverpool scientists have discovered how a protein linked to a severe form of childhood epilepsy is positioned within nerve cells, providing new insights into a rare genetic neurological disorder.

medical.title: Inner ear study challenges canonical understanding of hearing
medical.summary: New research offers a new understanding of how the inner ear processes sound, which could lead to improvements in hearing technology like cochlear implants.

medical.title: Can psychedelics improve decision-making?
medical.summary: For the one-in-five Americans with a mental health condition, the options for treatment aren't too much different from what they were half a century ago. Most medicines for psychiatric disorders were first pioneered in the 1950s.

medical.title: Custom MRI tool could show within weeks if pancreatic cancer treatment is working
medical.summary: About 60% of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer don't qualify for surgery because their disease is too advanced. For these patients, treatment typically begins with chemotherapy, in the hope that the tumor will shrink enough to be surgically removed, which offers the best chance of long-term survival. A new clinical trial at The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center—Arthur G. James Cancer Hospital and Richard J. Solove Research Institute (OSUCCC—James) is testing a custom imaging tool designed to measure much earlier whether that chemotherapy is working, so treatment can change quickly if it is not.

medical.title: Transgender consumers can face harm simply by trying to access everyday services, research finds
medical.summary: Transgender consumers can experience discrimination and psychological harm when carrying out everyday tasks such as changing their name, visiting a gym or accessing banking and health care, according to new research from the University of Bath.

medical.title: Open-source platform combines brain commands, spinal circuits and muscle responses in one simulation
medical.summary: Immense progress has been made in recent years in developing assistive systems for people who are paralyzed. However, the underlying neuromotor processes—from the brain's commands through the neural circuits in the spinal cord to the activation of the muscles—have so far been mostly studied in isolation. Researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) and their partners in Brazil have developed the MyoGen platform, which integrates these processes into a single simulation. The model, presented in the journal Nature Communications, is freely accessible and is intended to support both clinical research and the optimization of medical devices.

science.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
science.summary: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.

science.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds
science.summary: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than […]

science.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
science.summary: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.

science.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions
science.summary: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north.

science.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
science.summary: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).

science.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users
science.summary: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.

science.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms
science.summary: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before.

science.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
science.summary: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.

science.title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations
science.summary: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model can detect stress in agricultural crops using a nondestructive imaging technique, allowing changes in crop health to be monitored over time. Developed by a team of researchers at Penn State, the new model shows promise for accurately detecting crop stress caused by drought, disease, nutrient deficiency and other causes while using less computing power than some existing AI methods.

science.title: A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells
science.summary: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb.

science.title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss
science.summary: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. If glaciers border a lake, the water can melt the ice from underneath; furthermore, chunks of ice can break off and fall into the lake. The extent to which these processes influence the situation, compared with other factors, had not been sufficiently clarified at a global level until now.

science.title: X-ray technique advances temperature measurements under extreme pressure
science.summary: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have advanced the ability to measure temperatures in materials subjected to extreme pressures at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), providing new insights into how materials behave under conditions relevant to national security and high-energy-density physics.

science.title: Parasite protein expands understanding of how mitochondria build their ribosomes
science.summary: Mitochondria are essential components of the cells of most organisms, including humans. They are often referred to as the cell's powerhouses because they produce the energy needed for cellular functions. However, mitochondria originally evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells in the distant past.

science.title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale
science.summary: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale.

science.title: El Niño created a skiers' paradise in Chile—now it's Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies' turn
science.summary: El Niño has a reputation for being a skier's dream, bringing lots of snow to California's Sierra Nevada and the southern Rockies. Tahoe-area resorts were already seeing the effects in mid-November 2026 as several feet of snow fell and some resorts prepared to open early for the season. But El Niño's supercharged precipitation can spell trouble, too.

science.title: Practical organ-on-a-chip platform helps assess the toxicity of environmental chemicals
science.summary: Among the thousands of chemicals used in daily life, toxicity information is available for only a small fraction. Much of this information comes from high-dose animal studies, which are costly, time-consuming and limited by species differences.

science.title: Bumblebees challenge long-held beliefs about brain size and intelligence
science.summary: Bigger brains mean greater intelligence, or so conventional wisdom goes. After all, humans have much larger brains than most other animals and are generally considered the planet's most intelligent species.

science.title: Is it genuine love—or obsessive passion? Kierkegaard, the father of existentialism, had some thoughts
science.summary: Young love, honeymoon love, infatuation—these often feel spectacular. You have a burning need to be in constant contact, and you don't want to let that person out of your sight.

science.title: Clean energy choices shape environmental impacts beyond greenhouse gas emissions
science.summary: The burning of fossil fuels such as coal, gas and oil is the primary driver of climate change, but clean energy strategies to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions do not systematically alleviate other environmental problems. In fact, some pathways add pressure on natural resources like land, water and minerals.

science.title: Anthropic researcher says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, first posed in 1859
science.summary: A researcher at AI company Anthropic said Friday that he had used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

science.title: NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover Collects Samples
science.summary: This Nov. 16 collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. Learn more […]

environment.title: Could a short tail mean a new monkey species in Laos? Some scientists think so
environment.summary: There is no body. No genetic evidence — yet. There are just photos, but some scientists say those photos show a distinct enough primate to declare it a new species: the short-tailed langur, or Trachypithecus brevicaudus. The proposed species was described in the Vietnamese Journal of Primatology and lives in the Annamite Mountains of Laos. […]

environment.summary: Maribel Pacco grins as she recalls the first time she saw an Andean bear close-up in the wild. At the forest edge, a mother and her cubs browsed on bromeliads while the volunteer ranger watched for hours in awe. “I’m not a biologist, but at that moment, I decided to become a conservationist,” she says. […]

Friday marks the official end of this year’s two-week summit, known as COP31, which so far has failed to advance the drastic emission cuts needed to avert […]

environment.title: Japan looks to offshore wind to boost energy security, but hurdles remain
environment.summary: Japan has “tremendous potential” for offshore wind power, according to the national government and experts. But achieving that potential means overcoming major hurdles. While commercial-scale projects began coming online in recent years, the country still needs to address challenges that include refining its public-private partnerships, a buildout of related industries (such as turbine production), and […]

environment.title: Last Javan rhino habitat caught between mining plans and relocation debate
environment.summary: JAKARTA — Indonesian lawmakers and environmental groups are urging the government to revoke a mining map covering part of the waters around Ujung Kulon National Park, home to the world’s last surviving Javan rhinos. The calls were in response to a proposal by Hashim Djojohadikusumo, a mining and energy tycoon and the brother of President […]

environment.title: Fossil fuels’ role in Africa’s energy transition contested as UN climate conference closes
environment.summary: As the 2026 edition of the annual U.N. Climate Change Conference reaches its conclusion in Antalya, Türkiye, on Nov. 20, African governments are arguing for increased financial and technical support to respond to climate change. Top priorities include more money for protection of forests and other landscapes, funding to help vulnerable communities and economies adapt […]

environment.title: Nickel linked to deforestation in Indonesia traded on London Metal Exchange, says report
environment.summary: Two companies approved for trading nickel on the London Metal Exchange (LME) could be linked to supply chains that have cleared primary rainforest in Indonesia, according to a report published by the NGO Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA). The NGO investigated two LME-approved Indonesian refiners – PT CNGR Ding Xing and PT Eternal Nickel Industry (ENI) […]

environment.title: A mysterious 4,000-year-old wall is rewriting North Africa’s history
environment.summary: A remarkable 4,000-year-old defensive structure discovered in Morocco is rewriting what scientists thought they knew about ancient North African civilizations. The massive fortifications reveal unexpectedly sophisticated prehistoric societies and suggest that the region played a much greater role in Mediterranean history than previously recognized.

mix_items.title: Mental health diagnoses rise with medical complexity, chronicity in children
mix_items.summary: The prevalence of mental health (MH) diagnoses increases with increasing medical complexity and chronicity in Medicaid-enrolled children, according to a study published in Pediatrics.

mix_items.title: Flu vaccine effectiveness often weaker than advertised, study finds
mix_items.summary: New research suggests health officials may be overselling the protective power of the annual flu shot—but that doesn't mean folks should skip it, researchers added. The new analysis finds the influenza vaccine is often less protective than the 40% to 60% effectiveness against infection that's routinely stated, according to researchers from the University of Maryland.

mix_items.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
mix_items.summary: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.

mix_items.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds
mix_items.summary: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than […]

mix_items.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
mix_items.summary: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.

mix_items.title: Your genes might boost risk for high cholesterol
mix_items.summary: Frustrated that your cholesterol levels aren't budging for the better? You may have your genes to blame, a new study finds.

mix_items.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions
mix_items.summary: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north.

mix_items.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
mix_items.summary: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).

mix_items.title: Hair pulling, skin picking and nail biting are common in young people and cause significant distress
mix_items.summary: The study found that body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs), as they are known, can be a significant source of distress, particularly among young people who also experienced anxiety, depression and bullying.

mix_items.title: Less than half of TikTok videos on RSV prevention offer high-quality info, paper notes
mix_items.summary: Many people rely on social media to learn more about health conditions and trends. A study published in Vaccine that examined TikTok videos about respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention—including the maternal vaccine (Abrysvo) and the long-acting antibody nirsevimab (Beyfortus) for infants—finds that only 47% present high-quality information.

mix_items.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users
mix_items.summary: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.

mix_items.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms
mix_items.summary: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before.

mix_items.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
mix_items.summary: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.

mix_items.title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations
mix_items.summary: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model can detect stress in agricultural crops using a nondestructive imaging technique, allowing changes in crop health to be monitored over time. Developed by a team of researchers at Penn State, the new model shows promise for accurately detecting crop stress caused by drought, disease, nutrient deficiency and other causes while using less computing power than some existing AI methods.

mix_items.title: Researchers uncover the mechanisms of adhesion formation after thoracic surgery
mix_items.summary: Intrathoracic adhesions can develop after thoracic surgery and increase the risk of complications during repeat surgery. However, the detailed molecular mechanisms underlying their formation have remained unclear. In a Letter published in Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy, a team from Japan aimed to establish an animal model that closely reproduces pleural adhesions seen in patients and to identify key cells and signaling pathways involved in adhesion formation. The goal was to find new methods to prevent adhesions after thoracic surgery.

mix_items.title: A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells
mix_items.summary: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb.

mix_items.title: Patients give dental implants high marks after 40 years
mix_items.summary: Nearly 40 years after receiving dental implants and crowns, patients remain highly satisfied with how well they function. Their views on appearance are more mixed, according to a study from the University of Gothenburg, Sweden.

mix_items.title: Improved mapping reveals location of small molecules in the brain
mix_items.summary: Hsi-Chun Chao, a postdoctoral researcher at the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, developed a new methodology to map the locations of and differentiate nearly identical molecules in the brain.

mix_items.title: Metastatic pancreatic cancer responds well to treatment with combination of daraxonrasib and chemotherapy
mix_items.summary: Daraxonrasib combined with chemotherapy caused substantial tumor shrinkage in patients with pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body, according to new results from a Phase I/II clinical trial.

mix_items.title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss
mix_items.summary: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. If glaciers border a lake, the water can melt the ice from underneath; furthermore, chunks of ice can break off and fall into the lake. The extent to which these processes influence the situation, compared with other factors, had not been sufficiently clarified at a global level until now.

mix_items.title: Heart rhythm data reveal early signs of heart disease before conventional measures
mix_items.summary: The heart does not beat like a regular clock. Even at rest, the time between successive heartbeats continuously varies. Researchers at Tampere and Stanford universities have shown that the patterns of these subtle variations can reveal the early effects of cardiomyopathy, which is a hereditary heart disease. The paper is published in the journal Circulation: Arrhythmia and Electrophysiology.

mix_items.title: X-ray technique advances temperature measurements under extreme pressure
mix_items.summary: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have advanced the ability to measure temperatures in materials subjected to extreme pressures at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), providing new insights into how materials behave under conditions relevant to national security and high-energy-density physics.

mix_items.title: Parasite protein expands understanding of how mitochondria build their ribosomes
mix_items.summary: Mitochondria are essential components of the cells of most organisms, including humans. They are often referred to as the cell's powerhouses because they produce the energy needed for cellular functions. However, mitochondria originally evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells in the distant past.

mix_items.title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale
mix_items.summary: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale.

mix_items.title: Immune aging blueprint offers new clues to fighting cancer
mix_items.summary: A new study from Monash University has uncovered a genetic blueprint of immune aging, shedding light on why our bodies become less effective at fighting cancer and infections as we grow older. Published in Science Immunology, the preclinical study identified genetic changes that cause aging immune cells to become less effective, helping to explain why older people are more susceptible to cancer and experience more frequent and severe infections.

mix_items.title: Nearly half of adults over 70 benefited from exercise training across several areas of physical function
mix_items.summary: A yearlong exercise program improved physical function among adults aged over 70, but the benefits varied considerably between individuals. A study conducted at the University of Jyväskylä highlights that the success of exercise interventions should not be evaluated using a single outcome measure, as positive changes may occur in different aspects of physical function.

mix_items.title: Cell biologists uncover key mechanism behind a rare cause of childhood epilepsy
mix_items.summary: University of Liverpool scientists have discovered how a protein linked to a severe form of childhood epilepsy is positioned within nerve cells, providing new insights into a rare genetic neurological disorder.

mix_items.title: Inner ear study challenges canonical understanding of hearing
mix_items.summary: New research offers a new understanding of how the inner ear processes sound, which could lead to improvements in hearing technology like cochlear implants.

mix_items.title: Can psychedelics improve decision-making?
mix_items.summary: For the one-in-five Americans with a mental health condition, the options for treatment aren't too much different from what they were half a century ago. Most medicines for psychiatric disorders were first pioneered in the 1950s.

mix_items.title: El Niño created a skiers' paradise in Chile—now it's Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies' turn
mix_items.summary: El Niño has a reputation for being a skier's dream, bringing lots of snow to California's Sierra Nevada and the southern Rockies. Tahoe-area resorts were already seeing the effects in mid-November 2026 as several feet of snow fell and some resorts prepared to open early for the season. But El Niño's supercharged precipitation can spell trouble, too.

mix_items.title: Custom MRI tool could show within weeks if pancreatic cancer treatment is working
mix_items.summary: About 60% of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer don't qualify for surgery because their disease is too advanced. For these patients, treatment typically begins with chemotherapy, in the hope that the tumor will shrink enough to be surgically removed, which offers the best chance of long-term survival. A new clinical trial at The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center—Arthur G. James Cancer Hospital and Richard J. Solove Research Institute (OSUCCC—James) is testing a custom imaging tool designed to measure much earlier whether that chemotherapy is working, so treatment can change quickly if it is not.

mix_items.title: Transgender consumers can face harm simply by trying to access everyday services, research finds
mix_items.summary: Transgender consumers can experience discrimination and psychological harm when carrying out everyday tasks such as changing their name, visiting a gym or accessing banking and health care, according to new research from the University of Bath.

mix_items.title: Practical organ-on-a-chip platform helps assess the toxicity of environmental chemicals
mix_items.summary: Among the thousands of chemicals used in daily life, toxicity information is available for only a small fraction. Much of this information comes from high-dose animal studies, which are costly, time-consuming and limited by species differences.

mix_items.title: Bumblebees challenge long-held beliefs about brain size and intelligence
mix_items.summary: Bigger brains mean greater intelligence, or so conventional wisdom goes. After all, humans have much larger brains than most other animals and are generally considered the planet's most intelligent species.

mix_items.title: Open-source platform combines brain commands, spinal circuits and muscle responses in one simulation
mix_items.summary: Immense progress has been made in recent years in developing assistive systems for people who are paralyzed. However, the underlying neuromotor processes—from the brain's commands through the neural circuits in the spinal cord to the activation of the muscles—have so far been mostly studied in isolation. Researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) and their partners in Brazil have developed the MyoGen platform, which integrates these processes into a single simulation. The model, presented in the journal Nature Communications, is freely accessible and is intended to support both clinical research and the optimization of medical devices.

mix_items.title: Is it genuine love—or obsessive passion? Kierkegaard, the father of existentialism, had some thoughts
mix_items.summary: Young love, honeymoon love, infatuation—these often feel spectacular. You have a burning need to be in constant contact, and you don't want to let that person out of your sight.

mix_items.title: Clean energy choices shape environmental impacts beyond greenhouse gas emissions
mix_items.summary: The burning of fossil fuels such as coal, gas and oil is the primary driver of climate change, but clean energy strategies to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions do not systematically alleviate other environmental problems. In fact, some pathways add pressure on natural resources like land, water and minerals.

mix_items.title: Anthropic researcher says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, first posed in 1859
mix_items.summary: A researcher at AI company Anthropic said Friday that he had used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

mix_items.title: Where family foundations can help marine conservation
mix_items.summary: COP17 ended in Armenia amid disappointment over the lack of concrete measures to reduce biodiversity loss by 2030. Finance was a sore point. Philanthropy is only a small part of that picture, but foundations can take risks that public agencies often cannot. I think there are some particularly good opportunities for smaller foundations in […]

mix_items.title: Could a short tail mean a new monkey species in Laos? Some scientists think so
mix_items.summary: There is no body. No genetic evidence — yet. There are just photos, but some scientists say those photos show a distinct enough primate to declare it a new species: the short-tailed langur, or Trachypithecus brevicaudus. The proposed species was described in the Vietnamese Journal of Primatology and lives in the Annamite Mountains of Laos. […]

mix_items.summary: Maribel Pacco grins as she recalls the first time she saw an Andean bear close-up in the wild. At the forest edge, a mother and her cubs browsed on bromeliads while the volunteer ranger watched for hours in awe. “I’m not a biologist, but at that moment, I decided to become a conservationist,” she says. mix_items.summary: ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — Negotiators are still seeking concrete commitments for nations to transition away from fossil fuels, as this year’s U.N. climate summit reaches its final day. Friday marks the official end of this year’s two-week summit, known as COP31, which so far has failed to advance the drastic emission cuts needed to avert […]

mix_items.summary: This Nov. 16 collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. Learn more […]

mix_items.title: Japan looks to offshore wind to boost energy security, but hurdles remain
mix_items.summary: Japan has “tremendous potential” for offshore wind power, according to the national government and experts. But achieving that potential means overcoming major hurdles. While commercial-scale projects began coming online in recent years, the country still needs to address challenges that include refining its public-private partnerships, a buildout of related industries (such as turbine production), and […]

mix_items.title: Last Javan rhino habitat caught between mining plans and relocation debate
mix_items.summary: JAKARTA — Indonesian lawmakers and environmental groups are urging the government to revoke a mining map covering part of the waters around Ujung Kulon National Park, home to the world’s last surviving Javan rhinos. The calls were in response to a proposal by Hashim Djojohadikusumo, a mining and energy tycoon and the brother of President […]

mix_items.title: Fossil fuels’ role in Africa’s energy transition contested as UN climate conference closes
mix_items.summary: As the 2026 edition of the annual U.N. Climate Change Conference reaches its conclusion in Antalya, Türkiye, on Nov. 20, African governments are arguing for increased financial and technical support to respond to climate change. Top priorities include more money for protection of forests and other landscapes, funding to help vulnerable communities and economies adapt […]

mix_items.title: Nickel linked to deforestation in Indonesia traded on London Metal Exchange, says report
mix_items.summary: Two companies approved for trading nickel on the London Metal Exchange (LME) could be linked to supply chains that have cleared primary rainforest in Indonesia, according to a report published by the NGO Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA). The NGO investigated two LME-approved Indonesian refiners – PT CNGR Ding Xing and PT Eternal Nickel Industry (ENI) […]

mix_items.title: A mysterious 4,000-year-old wall is rewriting North Africa’s history
mix_items.summary: A remarkable 4,000-year-old defensive structure discovered in Morocco is rewriting what scientists thought they knew about ancient North African civilizations. The massive fortifications reveal unexpectedly sophisticated prehistoric societies and suggest that the region played a much greater role in Mediterranean history than previously recognized.
